courses.name: Electricity and Magnetism
courses.description: Comprehensive handbook covering Electrostatics, DC Circuits, Magnetism, Induction, Maxwell's Equations, and 200 CBT practice questions.

modules.title: Unit 1: Electrostatics & Electric Fields
modules.content:
Forces in Nature & Electrostatics

Covers the four fundamental forces, electric charge properties, Coulomb's Law, Electric Fields, Potential, Gauss's Law, and Capacitance.

play_circle Watch Complete Unit 1 Video Series

menu_book Read Full Unit 1 Notes
modules.feynman_prompt: Explain why like charges repel using the concept of electric fields.

flashcards.definition: F = k|q1q2|/r². Force between point charges is proportional to product of charges and inversely proportional to square of distance.
Charge exists only in discrete packets. q = ne, where e ≈ 1.602 × 10⁻¹ C.
Φ = Q_enc/ε₀. Electric flux through a closed surface is proportional to enclosed charge.

micro_quiz.question: Which fundamental force is responsible for holding protons and neutrons together in the nucleus?
micro_quiz.explanation: The Strong Nuclear Force overpowers the electromagnetic repulsion between protons in the nucleus.

micro_quiz.question: If you remove 1000 electrons from a neutral object, what is its net charge?
micro_quiz.explanation: Removing electrons (negative charge) leaves a positive charge. Q = 1000 × (+1.602×10⁻¹⁹ C) = +1.602×10¹⁶ C.

modules.title: Unit 2: DC Circuits & Components
modules.content:
Ohm's Law, Resistors & Diodes

Covers DC circuits, Ohm's Law, resistor combinations, EMF, internal resistance, thermionic emission, and rectification.

menu_book Read Full Unit 2 Notes
modules.feynman_prompt: Explain the difference between EMF and terminal voltage using a water pump analogy.

flashcards.definition: V = IR. Voltage equals current times resistance, provided temperature is constant.
Converting AC to DC using diodes. Full-wave is ~81.2% efficient, half-wave is ~40.6%.

micro_quiz.question: What is the efficiency of a full-wave rectifier?
micro_quiz.explanation: Full-wave rectifiers utilize both halves of the AC cycle, yielding ~81.2% efficiency.

modules.title: Unit 3: Magnetism & Magnetic Fields
modules.content:
Lorentz Force, Biot-Savart & Ampère

Covers magnetic fields, Lorentz force, Biot-Savart law, Ampère's law, magnetic dipoles, and dielectrics.

play_circle Watch Unit 3 Video
playlist_play Watch Complete Unit 3 Video Series

menu_book Read Full Unit 3 Notes
modules.feynman_prompt: Explain why a magnetic field does no work on a moving charge.

flashcards.definition: F = q(E + v × B). Total force on a charge in E and B fields.
Calculates magnetic field produced by a small current element.

micro_quiz.question: What is the SI unit of magnetic field (B)?
micro_quiz.explanation: Tesla (T) is the SI unit. 1 Tesla = 10,000 Gauss.

modules.title: Unit 4: Electromagnetic Induction
modules.content:
Faraday's Law & Transformers

Covers Faraday & Lenz's laws, self & mutual inductance, transformers, and eddy currents.

play_circle Watch Unit 4 Video

menu_book Read Full Unit 4 Notes
modules.feynman_prompt: Explain Lenz's Law using the concept of conservation of energy.

flashcards.definition: ℰ = -N(dΦ/dt). Induced EMF is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux.
E_s/E_p = N_s/N_p = I_p/I_s. Relates voltage, turns, and current in a transformer.

micro_quiz.question: Lenz's law is a consequence of conservation of:
micro_quiz.explanation: The induced current opposes the change to conserve energy. If it aided the change, it would create infinite energy.

modules.title: Unit 5: Maxwell's Equations & AC Circuits
modules.content:
EM Waves & RLC Circuits

Covers Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves, AC circuits, reactance, impedance, and resonance.

play_circle Watch Unit 5 Video

menu_book Read Full Unit 5 Notes
modules.feynman_prompt: Explain why light is considered an electromagnetic wave.

flashcards.definition: Four equations describing all classical electromagnetic phenomena. Predicts c = 1/√(µ₀ε₀).
f₀ = 1/(2π√(LC)). Occurs when X_L = X_C, making impedance Z = R (minimum).

micro_quiz.question: At resonance in a series RLC circuit, the impedance is:
micro_quiz.explanation: At resonance, X_L = X_C, so Z = √(R² + 0) = R (minimum impedance).
